correction.text: wide_mul_x86 is a schoolbook loop over _mulx_u64 and _addcarry_u64; it compiles to mulx + adc with zero adcx/adox, no inline assembly and no hand scheduling. The controlled comparison is Arch vs portable Solinas (mul 61.793 vs 82.885 ns, so mulx won 25.4%; ladder 422.821 vs 538.076 ns, 21.4%). The ~3x is Arch vs Mont (61.793 vs 20.662 ns, 2.991x) and belongs to the Solinas reduction, not to carry chains. A call to the out-of-line target-feature callee occurs once per field multiply. Hand-written ADX with paired adcx/adox carry chains has NOT been measured and is NOT_RUN. The mulx-plus-Montgomery-inlined experiment is already answered by PFP-48 (mulq 0, mulx 121, zero adcx/adox, every workload equal or slower); the hand-paired ADCX/ADOX question remains open.

provenance_decision.decision: Every performance kernel ships as the first-party portable Rust representation that has its own differential court and binary audit at a named artefact digest. The portable reference is retained as oracle and fallback. No third-party assembly (s2n-bignum, fiat-crypto or CryptOpt output) enters the custodian boundary in this row. The one architecture-specialised arm implemented for P-256 (p256::Arch, mulx/adcx on x86-64) is compiled but not selected because it lost to the portable Montgomery kernel on the admitted venue.
provenance_decision.section_8_route: docs/PERFORMANCE-FRONTIER.md §8 recommends fiat-crypto Rust as the portable reference and oracle, an s2n-bignum-grade assembly fast path (adopted or written and proved), and constant time as a separate obligation on the built DSO. That recommendation is recorded as the intended direction, not adopted: it is a decision for the project principal and no such code is in the tree.
rationale: The measured alternatives that exist on this hardware lost; selecting one would publish a measured regression (docs/PERFORMANCE-FRONTIER.md §11).
The portable kernels each have a differential court and a binary audit at a named digest; an architecture arm would require its own differential and audit at its own digest, and none exists.
Constant time is a separate obligation. No kernel has a mechanised proof; every kernel is NO_PROOF and the audits are review aids, not proofs.
Third-party assembly would add a new custodian boundary with no per-kernel evidence in this repository.

no_inheritance_rule: Evidence for one target, profile, compiler or artefact never transfers to another. Each kernel's differential court and audit are bound to the exact (target, profile, compiler, source, artefact digest) recorded here. A claim that cites evidence from a different identity is refused.
